question: Does reactive actor feedback specifically improve chest-impact recovery compared with replaying this actor's own time-varying quiet-standing commands?
intervention: Collect a 12-second live quiet sequence in the ball world for each of six actors on each backend. Replay its exact backend/pose-matched quiet commands after the final pre-launch frame, retaining live policy before that frame, unchanged PD/delay/physics, and quiet/+X/-X conditions at 5 kg / 1.4 m/s from 0.25 m.
admission: Live quiet must pass 8/8 on each backend. Native prefix tolerance 1e-10; GPU uses the previously locked calibration envelope. Replay original actor on each actual pre-switch observation (2e-6); post-switch live-world commands must exactly equal the saved quiet sequence. Require backend comparisons. Preserve every rejected admission.
decision: An impact-specific comparison requires admitted prefixes/backends and all replayed quiet cases retaining Stand. If quiet replay fails, the intervention remains confounded and no isolated impact-feedback claim is made. Changes in delivered impulses remain part of the encounter. No learning or promotion.
